app_documentation:
The Real-Time Inventory Management System is a modern, mobile-first application designed to streamline inventory operations for retail stores. Built with React for the frontend and Node.js/Express for the backend, the system leverages WebSocket technology to provide instant inventory updates across all connected devices. The application enables store personnel to quickly scan product barcodes using their mobile device cameras, view real-time stock levels, receive proactive low-stock alerts, and generate comprehensive sales reports. The PostgreSQL database architecture supports six core tables (users, suppliers, products, inventory, transactions, and alerts) that work together to maintain accurate inventory records and transaction history.

The system serves four distinct user roles: Store Clerks who perform daily inventory updates and barcode scanning, Store Managers who monitor stock levels and make ordering decisions, Store Owners who analyze business performance through sales reports, and Administrators who manage system configuration and user accounts. Key features include sub-2-second barcode scanning with automatic product lookup, real-time inventory synchronization that updates quantities immediately upon transaction completion, customizable low-stock threshold alerts sent via in-app notifications and email, comprehensive product management with supplier tracking, and interactive sales reporting with date range filtering and top-selling product analytics.

The application prioritizes speed and usability with a clean, card-based interface optimized for mobile devices. The bottom navigation provides quick access to five main sections: Home dashboard with quick stats and recent activity, Scan interface for camera-based barcode scanning, Alerts screen for managing low-stock notifications, Reports section for sales analytics and data export, and Settings for user preferences and threshold configuration. All interactive elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards with minimum 44x44px touch targets and 4.5:1 color contrast ratios.

Designed for single-store deployments, the system assumes standard retail barcode formats (UPC, EAN), requires user authentication for all operations, and handles concurrent transactions with proper database locking mechanisms. The mobile app supports both iOS and Android platforms with responsive layouts that adapt from 375px to 428px screen widths, while the web version provides additional breakpoints for tablet and desktop viewing. Performance optimizations include indexed database queries on frequently accessed columns, WebSocket connections for real-time updates without polling overhead, and on-demand report generation with configurable date ranges to minimize server load.

glossary.Barcode Scanning: The process of using a mobile device camera and Barcode Scanner API to capture and decode product barcodes (UPC, EAN formats) for instant product lookup and inventory updates, with a target response time of under 2 seconds from scan to product details display.
glossary.Real-Time Inventory Tracking: A WebSocket-based synchronization mechanism that instantly propagates inventory quantity changes across all connected client devices when transactions are completed, ensuring all users see current stock levels without manual refresh or polling delays.
glossary.Low Stock Threshold: A configurable minimum quantity value set per product in the inventory table that triggers automatic alert generation when current stock falls below this level, with default value of 10 units and customizable by Store Managers to match business-specific reorder points.
glossary.Transaction Types: Four categories of inventory movements recorded in the transactions table: 'sale' (customer purchase reducing stock), 'restock' (supplier delivery increasing stock), 'adjustment' (manual correction for discrepancies), and 'return' (customer return increasing stock), each creating an audit trail with user, timestamp, and quantity change.
glossary.Role-Based Access Control: A security model implemented at the application level that restricts feature access based on four user roles stored in the users table: Store Clerk (basic scanning and updates), Store Manager (alerts and product management), Store Owner (full reporting access), and Administrator (system configuration and user management).
glossary.WebSocket Connection: A persistent, bidirectional communication channel between the Node.js server and React clients that enables real-time push notifications for inventory updates, low-stock alerts, and transaction events without requiring clients to repeatedly poll the server for changes.
